title: Creating a project in a project-mode-billing org auto-provisions a SubscriptionProject and a Project Admin ProjectMember row
description: _provisionProjectBillingIfNeeded (project.controller.js) is called right after Project.createWithCode succeeds. For an org with billingMode:'project', it calls subscriptionService.provisionProjectSubscription, then — if the creator belongs to the org and is active — consumes a 'users' quota unit and creates a ProjectMember row for the creator with the system PROJECT_ADMIN role.
preconditions: subscriptionPlanId supplied in the create request
steps: Call POST /projects/:orgId with { name: 'Billed Project', subscriptionPlanId: <validPlanId> } as the creator user
expectedResult: A SubscriptionProject row exists for the new project with the given plan; a ProjectMember row exists linking the creator to the project with projectRoleId resolved to the system PROJECT_ADMIN role; grantBillingAdminsProjectAccess has additionally granted org billing admins access to the new project.

title: A billing provisioning failure during project creation rolls back the project, its ProjectMember row, and the consumed quota
description: The catch block in _provisionProjectBillingIfNeeded runs Promise.allSettled to delete the SubscriptionProject, ProjectMember rows, and the Project itself, and release the consumed 'projects' quota unit, then re-throws — 'Project-mode tenants must never retain a project without its billing row.'
steps: Call POST /projects/:orgId with a valid body and subscriptionPlanId while the subscription provisioning call is forced to fail
After the request returns its error response, query for the project by name and for any SubscriptionProject/ProjectMember rows referencing it
expectedResult: The API call fails with the underlying provisioning error; no Project, SubscriptionProject, or ProjectMember document exists afterward, and the org's consumed 'projects' quota has been released back (net zero change).

title: listByOrg attaches teamPreview/teamCount via a single batched ProjectMember query, not one query per project
description: listByOrg (project.controller.js) fetches ProjectMember.find({ projectId: { $in: projects.map(...) } }) exactly once regardless of how many projects are returned, then groups results into a Map keyed by projectId — avoiding the N+1 pattern the old embedded project.team field previously required.
preconditions: Org has 10 active projects, each with 1-3 ProjectMember rows
expectedResult: ProjectMember.find is called exactly once for the whole request (not 10 times); every returned project has a correct teamCount and a teamPreview array capped at 3 entries with firstName/lastName/avatar populated.

title: Dashboard aggregation scopes to resolveProjectIdsScope for a non-admin caller
description: exports.dashboard (project.controller.js) explicitly casts orgId to a real ObjectId for the aggregate $match (aggregate() does not auto-cast strings, unlike find()), and merges in resolveProjectIdsScope's project _id restriction for non-admins before running totalStats/statusStats aggregations.
preconditions: Org has 5 active projects; the calling user is a ProjectMember of only 2 of them and holds no project.admin
expectedResult: totalStats.totalProjects and statusStats counts reflect only the 2 projects the user is a member of — the other 3 org projects are excluded entirely from every aggregated number, and the call does not throw despite orgId being a string in the request.

title: addTeamMember consumes a 'users' quota unit only for project-mode orgs, never for org-mode orgs
description: addTeamMember checks isPricingV1Enabled(project.organizationId) AND org.billingMode === 'project' before calling quota.consume('users', 1, { projectId }). Org-mode orgs already counted this user once at User.create() time via user.controller.js, so this must stay gated to avoid double-counting.
preconditions: Two orgs: Org A (billingMode:'project'), Org B (billingMode:'org' / default)
steps: Add a new team member to a project in Org A and record the 'users' quota usage before/after
Add a new team member to a project in Org B and record the 'users' quota usage before/after
expectedResult: Org A's 'users' quota usage increments by 1 after the add. Org B's 'users' quota usage is unchanged by the add (it was already incremented when the user account was created).

title: listProjectsForUser returns every active org project for an admin bypass and only ProjectMember rows for everyone else
description: listProjectsForUser (projectAccess.js) is the source of GET /users/me/projects, which drives the frontend ProjectSelector and projectSlice.fetchProjects. computeProjectAccessForUser's isProjectAdmin short-circuit returns all active org projects with empty permissions/extraPermissions; a non-admin instead gets only their ProjectMember-backed projects fully annotated with resolved permissions.
preconditions: Org has 4 active projects and 1 archived project
Test user A holds project.admin; Test user B is a ProjectMember of exactly 1 of the 4 active projects
expectedResult: userA's result contains all 4 active projects (not the archived one), each with isProjectRoleAdmin:false and empty permissions arrays (admin bypass doesn't need per-project grants). userB's result contains exactly 1 project, annotated with their real projectRoleId and fully-resolved permissions.

title: A duplicate-key race on creationRequestId during concurrent retries still resolves to exactly one project and releases the extra quota reservation
description: If two requests bearing the same Idempotency-Key race past findIdempotentProject's initial check, the unique compound index unique_project_creation_request on {organizationId, creationRequestId} causes the second Project.createWithCode to throw code 11000; the catch path releases the just-consumed quota unit and re-resolves to the winning project via findIdempotentProject before responding 200 with idempotentReplay:true.
steps: Fire two concurrent POST /projects/:orgId requests with an identical Idempotency-Key and identical body
Inspect the org's 'projects' quota usage and the Project collection afterward
expectedResult: Exactly one Project document exists; the org's 'projects' quota was net-incremented by exactly 1 (not 2); one response is 201 and the other is 200 with idempotentReplay:true referencing the same project _id.
